transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM) — Maya Thompson (GHS Head of ML), Diego Alvarez (GHS Platform), Priya Narang (GHS Security), Ken Liu (GHS Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Purpose: sign off on pilot acceptance thresholds and agree on reporting format.
- Key go/no-go thresholds discussed: latency p95, token-per-second throughput, extraction accuracy, hallucination tolerance.
- Security and reporting: SOC 2 footprint, audit logs, SSO, KMS.
- Next: runbench week of Jul 20; Redwood to deliver runbook and CSV report template.

Topics (auto): acceptance thresholds, test payloads, reporting template, data access, security signoffs, timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight today, this is the pilot closure checkpoint to lock the acceptance metrics and the report template, um Sofia will run through the runbook then we'll confirm who owns what, okay?
[00:18] Maya Thompson: thanks Alex, yeah from our side we need to be explicit about pass/fail and what counts as an infra failure vs model failure, the audit team won't accept fuzzy wording.
[00:29] Sofia Patel: totally agree, so i built a draft spreadsheet — i'll share after — it has per-route thresholds and a final pass/fail column. high level we proposed: p95 latency <= 350ms for short-text generation (<=128 tokens) and p95 <= 900ms for long-form (512 tokens), throughput target 60 qps sustained for the dedicated pilot cluster, and extraction accuracy 92% on our labeled eval set.
[00:52] Ken Liu: 350ms p95 sounds good for our ux, is that end-to-end or just model inference? we need end-to-end since our app times include network and frontend rendering.
[01:05] Sofia Patel: good call — our thresholds are end-to-end from request ingress at Redwood endpoint to final token emitted. there is a separate column for model-only latency if you want to isolate kernel perf.
[01:16] Diego Alvarez: can we define the request shape? e.g., average tokens in, typical context window, KV cache warm vs cold? we saw wide variance in your earlier run.
[01:27] Sofia Patel: yes, runbook will include three payload families: short (prompt 40–120 chars, gen limit 128 tokens), mid (prompt ~300 chars, gen 256 tokens), long (prompt ~1k, gen 512 tokens). we'll do cold-start versus warmed KV cache, and then a sustained burst test at the throughput target.
[01:44] Maya Thompson: for accuracy metrics — what are you using? rouge/bleu? we need medically-relevant extraction so F1 on named-entity spans would be better.
[01:52] Sofia Patel: agreed, we recommend F1 for structured extraction tasks. for freeform summarization we'll include ROUGE-L as a secondary metric. we'll compute both and you'll set the primary gate: extraction F1 >= 0.92 on the labeled set.
[02:07] Priya Narang: security here — we need the run artifacts to include audit logs, request/response hashing, and no raw PHI left in logs. How will Redwood handle redaction and KMS?
[02:18] Jordan Lee: Redwood will support KMS integration for at-rest model artifacts and customer-provided keying for logs if required. for the pilot we suggest PHI-sanitized test data; real PHI should be gated until Private deployment with HSM.
[02:33] Priya Narang: sounds ok, prioritize log redaction and show us a sample audit export.
[02:38] Alex Kim: we'll include a sample audit CSV and a redaction checklist.
[02:42] Diego Alvarez: on reporting format: we prefer a machine-friendly CSV with every request row and a summarized dashboard slide deck. the CSV must include request_id, route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, extraction_f1, error_flag, hash_of_payload.
[02:59] Sofia Patel: that's exactly what the runbook template contains — we'll also deliver a Grafana snapshot and a one-page slides PDF summarizing pass/fail per route.
[03:12] Ken Liu: what's your suggested pass threshold for hallucination? we can't have freeform made-up facts in clinical context, even if extraction F1 is high.
[03:20] Sofia Patel: we propose automatic hallucination checks for entity consistency plus a human spot-check sample with zero-tolerance for clinically actionable hallucinations. automated tolerance is set to <=2% of sampled responses flagged for hallucination, and any clinically actionable hallucination is a hard fail.
[03:36] Maya Thompson: zero-tolerance for clinically actionable ones — agreed. define 'clinically actionable' in the runbook please.
[03:41] Sofia Patel: will do — we'll include examples and rubric.
[03:45] Alex Kim: timeline check — we need to finalize thresholds today so the run can be scheduled week of Jul 20. if any of you need adjustments, speak now.
[03:56] Diego Alvarez: we need 48-hour notice on maintenance windows for the pilot cluster, can Redwood guarantee dedicated capacity for the run windows?
[04:05] Sofia Patel: for the dedicated pilot cluster we can reserve capacity; we'll invoice the pilot reserved window per the SOW, and Redwood Dedicated guarantees no noisy neighbors for the run.
[04:16] Maya Thompson: what's the rollback policy if a run shows infra degradation?
[04:20] Sofia Patel: runbook includes automatic fallback to a lower-TPS, lower-cost variant and an immediate re-run plan. for acceptance the go/no-go is based on the latest completed clean run; if infra issues are detected we'll rerun after remediation.
[04:32] Ken Liu: about reporting cadence — immediate CSV after completion and a slide pack within 72 hours?
[04:36] Sofia Patel: yes, CSV within 24 hours of run completion, preliminary dashboard within 48 hours, full slide pack and narrative within 72 business hours.
[04:45] Diego Alvarez: for the CSV, please include a mapping of route names to our API endpoints.
[04:49] Alex Kim: we'll add a mapping sheet in the submission.
[04:52] Jordan Lee: a small note on metrics: please expect sampling noise. we'll run three sub-runs and you can take the median of p95 across runs for gating.
[05:03] Sofia Patel: good point — runbook prescribes three independent runs at the target load, median p95 used for gate, and any run with error-rate >1% invalidates that run.
[05:15] Maya Thompson: what about dataset size for accuracy? we can provide 1,200 labeled examples, is that sufficient?
[05:20] Sofia Patel: 1,200 is great; we'll specify a 300-sample random holdout for human spot check for hallucination review.
[05:28] Priya Narang: can Redwood redact before storing logs? we want only hashes and derived metrics retained.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: yes we can redact and only store hashes and metrics. for the pilot we recommend sanitized raw responses be kept in a temporary s3 with lifecycle 7 days, hashed and then deleted.
[05:46] Diego Alvarez: networking — we need a short checklist of firewall ports and egress rules.
[05:50] Sofia Patel: runbook has that, plus a VPC peering playbook. we'll also include a sample terraform snippet for peering if you want.
[05:59] Ken Liu: Ok on contract — Alex you mentioned sending a pilot SLA addendum?
[06:04] Alex Kim: yes, i'll send an addendum that lists the acceptance metrics, reserved run windows, reporting cadence, and pricing for pilot capacity. aiming to get that out today or tomorrow.
[06:11] Maya Thompson: one more question about model variants — if a variant meets latency but has slightly lower extraction F1, do we consider model-only rollback?
[06:20] Sofia Patel: the gate is per-route; you can accept different model variants per route as long as overall acceptance is met. we also support automatic routing policies to prefer the higher-accuracy variant while meeting latencies.
[06:33] Diego Alvarez: can we run quantized variants for cost reasons?
[06:36] Sofia Patel: yes, we'll include a quantized variant in the runbook; we'll report quality deltas and cost-per-1k-tokens for each variant.
[06:44] Ken Liu: perfect. anything else on metrics?
[06:47] Maya Thompson: hold on — we need to confirm the final pass/fail formula. is it: all critical routes must meet both p95 and extraction gates, and global error-rate < 0.5%?
[06:57] Sofia Patel: proposal: per-route hard gates: p95 <= threshold AND extraction F1 >= threshold. global error-rate must be <= 0.5% and hallucination automated flag <= 2% with human sample zero clinical hallucination. if any hard gate fails it's a no-go.
[07:13] Alex Kim: sounds like consensus. I'll state it in the addendum and the runbook.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: we'll also attach a sample CSV column definition and provide a JSON schema for the audit export.
[07:25] Priya Narang: please include SSO/SAML integration notes and SOC 2 artifact references for our auditors.
[07:31] Alex Kim: yes, will include SOC 2 report pointer and SSO steps.
[07:35] Sofia Patel: ok, quick recap of next steps — Sofia will publish runbook and CSV template by Jul 13, Maya to provide sanitized dataset and sample accounts by Jul 12, Diego to confirm networking and peering by Jul 15, Alex to share contract addendum by Jul 10, and we schedule runs week of Jul 20.
[07:53] Maya Thompson: that timeline works for us.
[07:56] Ken Liu: thanks — we'll review the runbook and get back with any adjustments within 48 hours.
[08:02] Alex Kim: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with attachments and the calendar for the run windows.

End of transcript.

Recap & explicit acceptance statement (auto):
- Acceptance is per-route and requires both latency and quality gates.
- Gate logic: median(p95 across 3 runs) <= threshold AND extraction F1 >= threshold AND global error-rate <= 0.5% AND hallucination automated flag <=2% with zero human-verified clinical hallucinations.
- Deliverables: runbook, CSV export (request-level rows), Grafana snapshot, slide deck narrative.
